decisions.statement: The pages written are the pages of that page type and of every page type beneath it.
A page naming its page type under the key already is passed over.
A field named beside the key is written inside each of that key's entries.
Those entries sit in the page's own body or in the entry file beside the page.
A run naming no field writes the key's own value.
A page type no page of which names a page by a bare name is refused.
A count handed in holds how many pages one run writes.
A run handed no count writes every page naming a page by a bare name.
One page refused refuses the whole change.
A refusal names the page that drew the refusal.
Writing the names anew is left to the mechanical change acting on a page type.
That change is reached through the runner rather than by an import.
Nothing here works out a body of its own.
Nothing here reads a page's own body.

definition: a bare name one key holds made an address, on every page of one page type
